causes.text: High inflation and economic uncertainties in 2023 caused shoppers to pull back on non-essential purchases such as furniture, jewelry and electronics, focusing instead on essential groceries. This shift in consumer behavior eroded sales of high-margin discretionary items at many retailers.

source_info.title: Costco misses quarterly earnings estimates as shoppers pull back

effects.text: On March 8, 2024, Costco's shares fell 7.6 %, its worst day since May 2022, after the company reported second-quarter revenue below analyst expectations. Lower gasoline prices contributed to the sales miss, and investors took the pullback in discretionary spending as a sign that growth was slowing.

source_info.title: Costco shares tumble after revenue miss

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Throughout 2023, persistent inflation and economic uncertainty led U.S. households to tighten budgets, particularly on big-ticket discretionary items. Consumers prioritized necessities over discretionary goods.
Costco, which sells high-margin categories like home furnishings and electronics, saw slower sales growth as shoppers traded down and deferred purchases.
When Costco posted second-quarter revenue below expectations on 2024-03-08, investors concluded the consumer slowdown was materially affecting results; the stock fell about 7.6 % that day.

rationale: Reduced discretionary spending due to inflation set the stage for Costco's revenue miss and the subsequent stock decline.
counterfactual_analysis: Had inflation cooled sooner and consumers maintained discretionary spending levels, Costco's revenue would likely have met or exceeded expectations and its stock may not have suffered a steep drop.

adversarial_confounders.text: Lower gasoline prices also contributed to the revenue miss and could explain part of the stock decline.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Makes it difficult to attribute the entire stock move to consumer spending alone.

details.commentary: High inflation and tighter household budgets made Costco's shoppers more selective, increasing their willingness to trade down or defer big-ticket purchases. This shift in buyer power pressured discretionary categories and contributed to the sales miss that investors punished with a sharp share-price decline.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Persistent inflation and macro uncertainty weighing on consumer spending
details.commentary: Elevated prices for essentials and uncertainty about the economic outlook curbed demand for higher-margin discretionary items. These macro conditions amplified the impact of Costco's softer results, leading markets to reassess near-term growth and margin assumptions.
